input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the constructor stores only self.multiplier and no longer sets self.initial, with no alias for the removed attribute
- failure path: code that reads wait.initial on a wait_exponential_jitter instance raises AttributeError, and code that assigns wait.initial = 2 is silently ignored because __call__ reads self.multiplier, so the configured wait never changes

Reviewer finding
- description: The `initial` attribute is replaced by `multiplier`, so existing code that reads `wait.initial` now raises AttributeError.
- rationale: Trigger: code or subclasses that access `wait_exponential_jitter(...).initial`. Mechanism: `self.initial` is no longer set, only `self.multiplier`. Impact: AttributeError at runtime. Because `initial` is only deprecated, this backward-compat break is probably unintended, but the attribute was likely rarely used publicly.
critique: The finding gives the same root cause as the label: the constructor no longer sets self.initial, only self.multiplier. It also gives the same main failure, an AttributeError when code reads wait.initial. It leaves out the silent-ignore-on-assignment part of the label, but the core defect and mechanism are the same.
